nameOverride.description: Override the chart name. Used as the prefix for all rendered resource names. Defaults to the chart name `bundle-analyzer`.

fullnameOverride.description: Fully override the rendered resource-name prefix, bypassing the chart-name + release-name composition. Use when you need exact control over generated names (rarely needed).

replicatedLicenseFields.description: Object populated by the Replicated platform at install time containing the license fields declared in the Vendor Portal. Not customer-configurable.

imagePullSecrets.description: Image pull secrets attached to every pod in the chart. Bundle Analyzer's default `enterprise-pull-secret` is added automatically when running through the Replicated platform; this list is for additional secrets only.

imageRegistry.description: Optional global registry override for all images. Do NOT set this if any Bitnami subchart is enabled — Bitnami uses `global.imageRegistry` differently and will clobber your subchart image registries. Prefer `global.proxyRegistry` for app images instead.

imagePullSecrets.description: Image pull secrets propagated to every pod in the chart, including subchart pods (Bitnami honors this via `global.imagePullSecrets`).

tag.description: Optional override that forces a specific tag on every app image (backend, worker, beat, frontend). Leave empty to let each component's `image.tag` fall back to `.Chart.AppVersion`, which is the recommended pattern (release version == image tag).

replicated.description: Container for values injected by the Replicated platform at install time (license, dockerconfigjson, etc.). Not customer-configurable; the SDK populates this.

appEnv.description: Application environment string passed to the backend pod as `APP_ENV`. Common values: `development`, `production`. Affects logging verbosity and a few feature defaults.

corsAllowedOrigins.description: Comma-separated list of origins permitted by the backend's CORS middleware. Use `*` for any origin (dev only). Set to your customer-facing domain in production, e.g. `https://bundle-analyzer.example.com`.

secretKey.description: Application session/CSRF signing secret. Auto-generated on first install by the chart and preserved across upgrades via the lookup-based secret contract; only override for tests or local dev where you need a known value.

jwtSecretKey.description: JWT signing key used by the backend for issuing access/refresh tokens. Auto-generated on first install and preserved across upgrades — overriding this on a running install will invalidate every customer's session.

allowRegistration.description: When `true`, the login page exposes the Create Account flow and `POST /api/v1/auth/register` accepts new users. When `false`, the Create Account tab is hidden and the endpoint returns 403. Controlled at install time via the EC config screen `Allow User Registration` field.

appBaseUrl.description: Canonical URL used by the backend when constructing absolute links in outbound emails (invitations, notifications). Should match how customers reach the frontend, e.g. `https://bundle-analyzer.example.com`.

proxyRegistry.description: Default registry path for app images when a per-image `registry` isn't set. Typically points at the Replicated proxy domain (`proxy.replicated.com` for stock installs, a custom domain like `images.bundlyzer.com` for custom-proxy deployments).

image.description: Image used by the `wait-for-deps` init container in backend/worker/beat pods. Defaults to a small Alpine image with `nc` for TCP readiness probing.

replicaCount.description: Number of backend FastAPI pods. Defaults to 1. Scale up if you have high concurrent API load; backend is stateless so scaling is safe.

tag.description: Backend image tag. Leave blank to fall back to `.Chart.AppVersion` — recommended pattern that keeps release version and image version in lockstep. Do NOT pin to `latest` in production.

service.description: Kubernetes Service for the backend. Default `ClusterIP` on port 8000; only change if you need direct external exposure (rare — the frontend usually fronts the backend).

resources.description: Standard Kubernetes resource requests/limits for the backend pod. Defaults are sized for ~10 concurrent bundle analyses; increase `limits.memory` if processing very large bundles (>200 MB).

email.description: Email address for the bootstrap admin account created at install time. The chart will fail to create a usable install if this AND `allowRegistration` are both empty/false.

password.description: Initial password for the bootstrap admin account. Paired with `bootstrapAdmin.email`. Operators should change this through the in-app account settings after first login.

aiEnabled.description: License-gated string-valued flag (`'true'` or `'false'`) injected from the customer license's `ai_chat_enabled` field via `helmchart.yaml`. The backend reads this to enable/disable the `/api/v1/findings/explain` endpoint.

defaultEmailNotificationsEnabled.description: Install-time default for whether email notifications are enabled in the in-app Notification Settings page on first install. Admins can override later via the UI; the chart value is seed-only.

defaultEmailRecipients.description: Comma-separated list of email addresses pre-filled in the in-app Notification Settings on first install. Empty by default. Seed-only — does not override user edits.

defaultSlackNotificationsEnabled.description: Install-time default for whether Slack notifications are enabled in the in-app Notification Settings page on first install.

defaultSlackWebhookUrl.description: Incoming-webhook URL pre-filled in the in-app Notification Settings on first install. Should be a `https://hooks.slack.com/services/...` URL generated by adding an Incoming Webhooks integration to a Slack channel.

defaultNotifyOnSeverities.description: Comma-separated finding severities that trigger notifications on first install. Valid values: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `info`. Default: `critical,high`.

aiModel.description: Anthropic model ID used by the backend's AI explanation feature. Defaults to `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`. Customers can rotate the model without redeploying via `kubectl set env deploy/bundle-analyzer-backend BACKEND_AI_MODEL=<new-model>`.

maxBundleSizeMb.description: Maximum support-bundle upload size in megabytes. The backend rejects uploads larger than this with HTTP 413. Default is 500 MB. Bundle Analyzer is bottlenecked by this on memory-constrained installs — set it lower (e.g., 100) if you're running on a 2-CPU, 4-GB VM and seeing the worker OOMKill while processing large bundles.

dbPoolSize.description: SQLAlchemy connection pool size (steady-state). Default 5. Match to your Postgres `max_connections` divided by the number of backend + worker replicas.

dbPoolOverflow.description: SQLAlchemy connection pool overflow (temporary burst above `dbPoolSize`). Default 10. Combined with `dbPoolSize: 5` yields 15 max concurrent connections per backend pod, which fits the embedded Bitnami Postgres defaults.

rateLimitUpload.description: SlowAPI rate-limit string for the bundle-upload endpoint, applied per source IP. Default `10/minute`. Tighten for multi-tenant deployments; loosen for trusted internal networks.

rateLimitAi.description: SlowAPI rate-limit string for the AI-explain endpoint, applied per source IP. Default `20/minute`. AI calls cost real money — keep this conservative.

metricsEnabled.description: When `true`, the backend reports custom metrics (bundles uploaded, findings count, etc.) to the Replicated SDK sidecar. Default `true`; disable only for true offline air-gap installs that want zero outbound telemetry.

replicaCount.description: Number of Celery worker pods. Scale up when bundle-processing backlog grows. Workers are stateless so scaling is safe. Don't scale `beat` past 1 (see `beat.replicaCount`).

resources.description: Resource requests/limits for the Celery worker. Default 1 vCPU / 1 GiB; increase memory if processing very large bundles.

replicaCount.description: Number of Celery beat scheduler pods. MUST remain at 1. Multiple beats produce duplicated periodic-task firings (rate limit checks, retention purges, license re-validation). The schema's `minimum: 1` enforces the floor; you should not raise above 1.
Number of frontend nginx pods serving the React SPA. Default 1; scale up only if you have very high concurrent web traffic — the frontend is just serving static assets, not doing computation.

backendUrl.description: URL the frontend uses to reach the backend API. Leave empty to use the in-cluster Service DNS name (`http://bundle-analyzer-backend:8000`). Override only if the frontend runs outside the cluster (e.g. served from a CDN), in which case point at the public backend URL.

postgresql.description: Bitnami PostgreSQL subchart configuration. When `postgresql.enabled` is `true`, the chart deploys an embedded Postgres. The application user password is auto-generated by the chart and preserved across upgrades. See Bitnami's chart docs for the full set of subchart values.

host.description: DNS hostname or IP of an external PostgreSQL server, used when `postgresql.enabled` is `false`. Must be reachable from inside the Kubernetes cluster.

port.description: TCP port of the external PostgreSQL server. Default 5432.

username.description: PostgreSQL role Bundle Analyzer will connect as. Must already exist with full privileges on the `database` named below.

password.description: Password for the external PostgreSQL role. Stored as a Kubernetes Secret in the bundle-analyzer namespace.

database.description: Name of the existing PostgreSQL database Bundle Analyzer will connect to. The chart does NOT create the database — it must exist before install.

redis.description: Bitnami Redis subchart configuration. Redis is the Celery broker + result backend; required for worker/beat to function. The chart does not currently support pointing at an external Redis.

replicated.description: Replicated SDK subchart configuration. The SDK runs as a sidecar to the backend and handles license validation, custom metrics reporting, and update notifications.

enabled.description: Toggle for whether to deploy the embedded MinIO StatefulSet for bundle tarball storage. Default `true`; only disable if pointing at an external S3-compatible store (not currently supported by the chart).

accessKey.description: MinIO root access key. Auto-generated to a random value on first install via the chart's secret contract and preserved across upgrades; only override for local dev where you need a known value.

secretKey.description: MinIO root secret key. Auto-generated on first install and preserved across upgrades — overriding on a running install will rotate the credential and break the backend's connection until pods restart with the new value.

bucket.description: MinIO bucket name where bundle tarballs are stored. Default `bundles`. Created automatically on first install.

enabled.description: When `true`, MinIO data lives on a PersistentVolumeClaim. Default `true`. Disabling makes the install non-persistent — bundle tarballs are lost on pod restart.

size.description: Requested PVC size for MinIO bundle storage. Default 10Gi. Each support bundle is typically 5-50 MB, so 10Gi holds a few hundred bundles. Increase based on retention policy.

storageClassName.description: Explicit StorageClass name for the MinIO PVC. Leave empty to use the cluster's default StorageClass.

enabled.description: When `true`, the chart creates a Kubernetes Ingress for the frontend. Default `false` — most installs use NodePort or port-forward access during early evaluation.

className.description: Ingress class name (e.g. `nginx`, `traefik`). Required when `enabled: true`; without it, no Ingress controller will claim the resource.

annotations.description: Free-form Ingress annotations. Use for cert-manager hints, SSL redirects, body size limits, etc.

enabled.description: When `true`, the chart adds the `cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer` annotation to the Ingress so cert-manager auto-issues a real TLS cert. Mutually exclusive with `generateSelfSignedCert: true`.

clusterIssuer.description: Name of the cert-manager ClusterIssuer to use (e.g. `letsencrypt-prod`). Required when `certManager.enabled: true`.

generateSelfSignedCert.description: When `true`, the chart generates a self-signed TLS cert via `tls-secret.yaml` on first install and never overwrites it on upgrades (preserved via Helm `lookup` + `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`). For production, set `false` and use `certManager.enabled` instead.

regenerateSelfSignedCert.description: When `true`, forces regeneration of the self-signed cert on upgrade even if one exists. Use only when intentionally rotating the cert; will invalidate any cached cert pins in customer browsers.
